title: Connectors & Discourse Markers
description: Master connectors for Grade 9: addition, contrast, reason, result, sequence, illustration and summary markers, with punctuation rules — bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: Categories of Connector
topics.concept:
Connectors group by the relationship they show:

CategoryExamples
Additionand, also, besides, moreover, furthermore, in addition, not only…but also
Contrastbut, however, yet, though, although, even though, despite, on the contrary, nevertheless
Reason / Causebecause, since, as, due to, owing to, on account of
Result / Effectso, therefore, thus, hence, consequently, as a result
Conditionif, unless, provided, as long as, in case
Sequencefirst, then, next, after that, subsequently, finally, lastly
Illustrationfor example, for instance, such as, namely
Summaryin short, in brief, to conclude, to sum up, in other words

examples.problem: Choose a connector: It was raining; ___, we cancelled the trip.
examples.solution: therefore / so / as a result — a result connector fits the consequence.

examples.problem: Choose a connector: He is rich; ___, he is unhappy.
examples.solution: however / nevertheless / yet — a contrast fits the surprising idea.

topics.title: Punctuating Connectors
topics.concept:
How you punctuate depends on the type of connector:

  • Coordinating conjunctions (and, but, so, or): a comma before them when joining two clauses — She tried, but she failed.
  • Subordinating conjunctions (because, although, when): no comma if the main clause is first; a comma if the subordinate clause is first — Although it rained, we played.
  • Conjunctive adverbs (however, therefore, moreover, nevertheless): use a semicolon before and a comma after when joining two clauses — He was tired; however, he continued. At the start of a sentence, just a comma after — However, he continued.

Don't double up: avoid 'Although … but …' or 'Because … so …' — one connector is enough.

examples.problem: Punctuate: It was late however we kept working.
examples.solution: It was late; however, we kept working. — semicolon before, comma after 'however'.

examples.problem: Fix: Although he was ill, but he came.
examples.solution: Although he was ill, he came. — don't use 'although' with 'but'.

recap: Conjunctive adverb (however/therefore): semicolon before, comma after

questions.q: Punctuate: 'He is rich however he is sad.'
options: He is rich, however he is sad.
He is rich; however, he is sad.
He is rich however; he is sad.

questions.q: Which fits? 'Sports, ___ football and tennis, build teamwork.'
Choose: 'Although he was poor, ___ he was generous.'
questions.explanation: 'Although' already contrasts; no extra connector is needed.

questions.q: Choose the best connector: 'The project was complex; ___ , the team completed it ahead of schedule.'
Spot the error: 'Despite of the rain, the match continued.'

options: She studied; moreover she practised daily.
She studied; moreover, she practised daily.
She studied, moreover she practised daily.
She studied moreover; she practised daily.

questions.q: Choose the connector that fits: 'He did not prepare; ___ , he failed the interview.'
Fill in: 'Not only ___ he sing, but he also dances.'
questions.explanation: After fronted 'Not only', invert: 'Not only does he sing …'.

questions.q: Which connector wrongly suits the meaning? 'The food was delicious; ___ , the service was poor.'
questions.explanation: The link is contrast, so 'therefore' (result) is wrong.

questions.q: Rearrange and punctuate: 'cold / it / was / nevertheless / out / we / went / ;'
options: It was cold; nevertheless, we went out.
It was cold, nevertheless we went out.
It was cold nevertheless; we went out.
Nevertheless it was cold; we went out.

questions.q: Choose the most precise summary marker: 'The evidence is clear, the witnesses agree, and the timeline fits. ___ , he is guilty.'

intro.en: Connectors (also called discourse markers, linkers or transitions) are the signposts of writing. They tell the reader how one idea relates to the next — whether you are adding, contrasting, giving a reason, or drawing a conclusion. Used well, they turn a list of sentences into a smooth, logical argument.
intro.hi: संयोजक (connectors) — जिन्हें discourse markers, linkers या transitions भी कहते हैं — लेखन के दिशा-सूचक हैं। ये पाठक को बताते हैं कि एक विचार अगले से कैसे जुड़ा है — आप जोड़ रहे हैं, विरोध कर रहे हैं, कारण दे रहे हैं, या निष्कर्ष निकाल रहे हैं। सही प्रयोग से वाक्यों की सूची एक सहज, तार्किक तर्क बन जाती है।

real_life.situation:
Compare two versions of advice:

Choppy: Exercise daily. You will feel fresh. You will sleep well.

Linked: Exercise daily; as a result, you will feel fresh, and moreover, you will sleep well.
real_life.why: The connectors 'as a result' and 'moreover' show the reader that the second and third ideas are a consequence and an addition. Good connectors make the logic visible — that's why every essay needs them.

rule_box.formula: Pick the connector that matches the LOGICAL link between ideas
rule_box.example: He studied hard; therefore, he passed. He was tired; however, he continued.

quick_test.explanation: 'however' signals a contrast between two ideas.

common_mistakes.wrong: He was tired, however he continued.
common_mistakes.right: He was tired; however, he continued.
common_mistakes.note: Use a semicolon before and a comma after 'however'.

common_mistakes.wrong: It rained, moreover the match was cancelled.
common_mistakes.right: It rained; therefore, the match was cancelled.
common_mistakes.note: The link is result, not addition.

reading.passage: Cities are growing fast. As a result, traffic has increased sharply. Moreover, pollution levels are rising. However, some solutions exist. For example, cycle lanes and electric buses reduce emissions. Therefore, with proper planning, cities can grow without harming the environment. In short, growth and greenery can go together.

questions.q: List one connector each for result, addition and contrast from the passage.

questions.answer: 'For example' — an illustration marker introducing cycle lanes and electric buses.
'In short' — a summary marker that closes the paragraph.

speaking: He worked hard; therefore, he succeeded.
It was expensive; however, it was worth it.
We stayed in because it was raining.
First we planned, and finally we acted.
Many sports, such as cricket and hockey, are popular.

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph (5 sentences) on any topic, using at least one connector of addition, contrast, reason, result and summary, punctuated correctly.
writing.example: Reading is useful. Moreover, it is enjoyable. However, many avoid it. Therefore, we should encourage it. In short, books are friends for life.
